text:
The only failure is CMRR, at 57.4 dB against a 60 dB target. The cause is the tail device MT, which is at the edge of saturation: only 14 mV of headroom (Vds − Vdsat), so its output resistance is low (gm/gds ≈ 9). The topology itself is fine.

Three changes give the tail more headroom and a higher output resistance:
- Raise the tail gm/Id (`gmidt`) to cut its saturation voltage.
- Raise the diff-pair gm/Id (`gmid1`) to lower its Vgs, which lifts the tail node.
- Lengthen the tail device (`Lt`).

This is a parameter change, so a refine is enough.

```json
{"action": "refine",
 "reason": "Only CMRR fails because tail MT sits at edge of saturation (0.014 V margin). Higher gmidt (lower Vdsat), higher gmid1 (lower Vgs, higher tail node) and longer Lt raise tail Rout. Topology is adequate; refine with widened bounds.",
 "params": {"gmid1": 21.0, "L1": 2.0, "gmid3": 10.5, "L3": 2.0, "Itail": 7.8e-6, "gmidt": 11.0, "Lt": 3.0},
 "bounds": {"gmid1": [17.0, 24.0], "gmidt": [8.0, 15.0], "Lt": [2.0, 5.0], "Itail": [6.5e-6, 8.2e-6], "gmid3": [8.0, 13.0]}}
```
